provenance: The facts on the twelveswaras raaga pages: scales, parents and note sets checked against published sources (corrections and their sources in raaga_corrections.json); not reviewed by a musician. Positions count semitones from Sa (0-11).

raagas.name: Aṭāna
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M1 P G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of valour and defiance: martial, zig-zag phrases (P M P G R), as in Tyagaraja's 'Ela Nee Daya Raadu'.
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R (chatusruti rishabha R2), P (panchama) and N (kakali nishada N3) are the vital/emphasised notes; an uttaranga-pradhana raga that does not go much below madhyama.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Shadja (S) and Panchama (P), on which Atana typically resolves in the upper register.

raagas.name: Behāg
raagas.parent: 29 Dheera Shankarabharanam (sources place Behag under Shankarabharanam, NOT Harikambhoji)
raagas.arohanam: S G3 M1 P N3 D2 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A soft, romantic raaga: the sweetness of 'Suttum Vizhi Sudar' (Kandukondain Kandukondain) and Lalgudi's beloved Behag thillana.
raagas.confused_with: Bihag (Hindustani); Khamas
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G3 and N3 (Ga = vadi, Ni = samvadi of the parent Bihag; N3 kakali nishada is prominent and is typically the note from which alapana/tanam is launched).
raagas.nyasa_swaras: S, G3, P, N3 (phrases resolve chiefly to S, with G3, P and N3 as sustained landing notes; R2 and D2 are never rested upon).

raagas.name: Bhairavi
raagas.parent: Natabhairavi (20th melakarta); bhashanga janya that borrows chatushruti dhaivatam (D2) from Kharaharapriya
raagas.arohanam: S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: One of the grandest raagas: the 'Viriboni' Ata-tala varnam every student learns; deep, devotional, tinged with pathos (karuna).
raagas.confused_with: Mukhari ('Bhairavi is distinguished from Mukhaari'); also Manji and Huseni
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Nishada (N2, kaisiki) is an important jeeva swara, rendered with varying degrees of gamaka; gandhara (G2) and the two dhaivatas (D2/D1) are the notes whose gamaka handling gives the raga its flavour.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Panchama (P) is the purna (full) nyasa swara, on which one may sustain at length; chatusruti dhaivata (D2) is an alpa (minor) nyasa used to conclude phrases without stress, e.g. tara-sthayi S n d and R S n d.

raagas.name: Bilahari
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 P D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A bright, auspicious raaga of joy and celebration; sunny, upward-lifting phrases, often opens concerts and sounds at weddings.
raagas.confused_with: Mohanam (shares the pentatonic ascent); also Shankarabharanam, Mohanakalyani, Garudadhvani, Desakshi
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R, D, N (chatushruti rishabha R2, chatushruti dhaivata D2, kakali nishada N3).
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R2), Panchama (P) and Dhaivata (D2).

raagas.name: Bēgaḍa
raagas.arohanam: S G3 R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2 D2 P S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A gently smiling, majestic raaga of winding zig-zag phrases, heard in Tyagaraja's 'Nadopasana'; graceful rather than grave.
raagas.confused_with: Shankarabharanam (same parent mela; beginners slide into it if the P D N D P phrase is not kept crisp)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Dhaivata (D2) emphasised as the life/defining note, secondary source
raagas.nyasa_swaras: N (nishada) is an important resting point, with a characteristic resting gamaka at N in phrases like pdp N, D, p and N dpmgr.

raagas.name: Dhanyāsi
raagas.parent: Janya of 8th melakarta Hanumatodi (Dikshitar school derives it from 20th melakarta Natabhairavi)
raagas.arohanam: S G2 M1 P N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A plaintive bhakti raaga, Tyagaraja's 'Sangeetha Gnanamu'; listen for its soulful, winding descent (S N D P M G R S).
raagas.confused_with: Suddha Dhanyasi / Udayaravichandrika (symmetric pentatonic = Dhanyasi's arohana notes); Salaga Bhairavi; compared with Todi
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G, N (sung with kampita gamakam)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: P (per karnatik.com)

raagas.name: Dēvagāndhāri
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: Arabhi's softer twin: a prayerful, slow-moving raaga of Tyagaraja's 'Ksheera Sagara Sayana'; listen for its gamaka-rich descent.
raagas.confused_with: Arabhi (identical basic arohana/avarohana; Devagandhari differs by gamakas, elongated G3 and the N2 bhashanga usage). Name-confused with Devamanohari
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Rishabha (R2), Gandhara (G3) and Dhaivata (D2) are the ragachaya (identity) svaras; the gamaka-laden rishabha and elongated (deergha) gandhara are the defining features.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R2), Panchama (P) and Dhaivata (D2).

raagas.name: Gauḷa
raagas.arohanam: S R1 M1 P N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 P M1 R1 G3 M1 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of Dikshitar's 'Sri Maha Ganapati Ravatu Mam': an angular, auspicious Ghana raga invoking Ganesha at a concert's opening.
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R1 (ekasruti / gaula rishabha) is the key life-note carrying the raga's grave bhava, assisted by S (shadja) and N3 (kakali nishada).
raagas.nyasa_swaras: R1, and the region around M P N to which the raga always returns.

raagas.name: Harikāmbhōji
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The 28th melakarta and parent scale of Mohanam, Kambhoji and Khamas, heard in Tyagaraja's 'Dina Mani Vamsa'; warm and expansive.
raagas.confused_with: Its janyas Kambhoji, Mohanam, Yadukula Kambhoji, Kedaragaula, Kamas, Natakurinji, Sahana, Surutti, Andolika; also Vachaspati (its prati-madhyama 64th-mela counterpart)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: N2 (kaisiki nishada) and M1 (madhyama); R2 and N2 are the two notes that carry the characteristic oscillation.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: G3 and D2 (nyasa swaram ga, dha); graha swara S.
film_songs: Kannukku Mai Azhaghu (Tamil, listed as the cine-song example on Raga Surabhi)

raagas.name: Hussēnī
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G2 M1 P N2 D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A tender, plaintive raaga, a rare phrase-oriented cousin of Bhairavi, recognised by its wistful, gamaka-laden phrases around the gandhara.
raagas.confused_with: Bhairavi, Mukhari, Anandabhairavi (distinguished by its sharp steady chatushruti dhaivatam vs Mukhari's shuddha dhaivatam, and by 'ri ga ma ga ri sa')
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R2 (rishabha) and P (pancama); rishabha is especially important and typically elongated or parked on. Elongated ri and pa immediately establish the ragabhava.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: S and P are the principal resting/parking notes (phrases sa-pa-Sa, sa sa pa pa); ri is also frequently held. No source uses the formal term nyasa for Huseni explicitly (inferred from resting behavior).

raagas.name: Kalyāṇi
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The queen of raagas, Ilaiyaraaja's 'Janani Janani'; bright and grand, built entirely on sharp notes (Hindustani Yaman).
raagas.confused_with: Shankarabharanam (same notes but different gamaka treatment); also compared with Vachaspati and Lathangi
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Ga and Ni (per Subbarama Dikshitar, Ri and Ga are the jiva swaras; Ni is also prominent)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Ri, Ga, Dha and Ni (all swaras except Ma can serve as nyasa swaras)

raagas.name: Kamās
raagas.arohanam: S M1 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of the beloved 'Brochevarevarura': warm and romantic (sringara), a late-night favourite for javalis and love songs.
raagas.confused_with: Khamaj (Hindustani); Nattakurinji
raagas.jeeva_swaras: M1 (madhyama) and D2 (dhaivata), an uttaranga-pradhana raga.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: M1 is the primary resting note, rendered as (G3)M1; P (panchama) also used as nyasa.

raagas.name: Karaharapriya
raagas.parent: 22nd melakarta (Kharaharapriya), it is itself the 22nd melakarta, not a janya
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of Tyagaraja's 'Chakkani Raja Margamu': a majestic, expansive full-octave scale (the 22nd melakarta) rich in sweeping phrases.
raagas.confused_with: Hemavati (its prati-madhyamam / 58th melakarta counterpart)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R2 (ri) and P (pa) are the amsa/predominant (sonant) svaras; the raga's chaya (identity) notes are ri, ga, dha, ni.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: R2, G2, D2, N2 (ri, ga, dha, ni), listed together as the chaya and nyasa svaras.

raagas.name: Kāmavardani
raagas.parent: 51st Melakarta – Kamavardhini (also called Pantuvarali); prati madhyama counterpart of the 15th mela Mayamalavagowla
raagas.arohanam: S R1 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The poignant morning raaga of Ilaiyaraaja's 'Roja Vai Thalattum' (Pantuvarali): pensive, devotional, all-sharp with a plaintive edge.
raagas.confused_with: Poorvikalyani (sounds similar, differs in dhaivata swara); also compared with Varali and Shubha Pantuvarali (different gandharam)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G, D, M, P (per Subbarama Dikshitar, Sangeetha Sampradaya Pradarshini)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: S, R, G, M, P, N, of which R, G and M are hrswa (short) nyasa swaras

raagas.name: Kānaḍa
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G2 M1 D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 P M1 G2 M1 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The majestic, Hindustani-derived raaga of Tyagaraja's 'Sri Narada': listen for its serious, weighty, zig-zag phrases (gravitas).
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Gandhara (G2) is the raga's defining/identity note (singing it alone would suffice); the rishabha (R2) is cited as the jiva svara of the mela-22 family.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Beyond the universal Shadja (S) and Panchama (P), the distinctive nyasa svaras are Rishabha (R2), Gandhara (G2) and Dhaivata (D2).

raagas.name: Kāpi
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 N2 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of 'Kanne Kalaimane' (Moondram Pirai) and Purandaradasa's 'Jagadodharana': soft, tender, pleading, devotional.
raagas.confused_with: Hindustani Kafi/thaat and raag Pilu; Desh
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Gandhara (G2) and Rishabha (R2); per the SSP the gandhara and rishabha are the jiva and nyasa svaras, and the elongated/oscillated ga is the strongest identity note.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R2) and Gandhara (G2) (the SSP names gandhara and rishabha as both jiva and nyasa).

raagas.name: Kāṁbhōji
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of Tyagaraja's grand 'O Rangasayee' and the concert-favourite 'Kaana Kann Kodi Vendum': majestic, expansive sweep.
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Chaya/jeeva swaras are M1 (madhyama), D2 (dhaivata) and N2 (nishada); the raga's identity also leans on S R G P D.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: G3, M1, P, D2 (ga, ma, pa, dha).
film_songs: Aarupadai Veedu Konda (listed as a film example for Kambhoji on ragasurabhi.com

raagas.name: Kēdāragauḷa
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A breezy morning raaga of many moods, heard in Tyagaraja's 'Venugana Loluni' (rendered by MS Subbulakshmi); bright and free-flowing.
raagas.confused_with: Madhyamavati (identical ascending notes S R2 M1 P N2 S); Narayanagowla; Vivardhini; Yadukulakamboji; Surutti
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Rishabha (R2) and Nishada (N2) are the ragachaya (identity) svaras; the elongated, heavily oscillated rishabha is the signature.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R2) and Panchama (P); Shadja (S) is also a common landing.

raagas.name: Madhyamāvati
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 P M1 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The auspicious raaga concerts traditionally close on (the Mangalam), heard in Tyagaraja's 'Ramakatha Sudha'; a bright, protective mood.
raagas.confused_with: Manirangu and Brindāvana Sāranga (scale-similar); graha bhedam relates it to Mohanam, Hindolam, Shuddha Sāveri
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R2 (chatushruti rishabha) and N2 (kaisiki nishada) are the life/identity notes (Ri always oscillated, Ni kampita); one source adds M1, listing R, M, N.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: R, M, N (per carnaticmusicexams.in, the same set it calls jeeva/chaya). No primary lakshana-grantha statement of the nyasa swaras was located.
songs: Aadaadu Asangaadu Vaa, Oothukkadu Venkata Subbaiyer

raagas.name: Mukhāri
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N2 D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The classic raaga of grief and pathos, Tyagaraja's 'Entani Ne'; famed for its power to move listeners to tears.
raagas.confused_with: Bhairavi (esp.), Huseni, Salagabhairavi, Kokilavarali, Maanji (allied ragas)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Rishabha (R2), Madhyama (M1) and Nishada (N2) are the ragachaya (character-defining) svaras; stress falls on Madhyama (e.g. S R M G R S) and shifts to Rishabha (e.g. P D S R). Sources use 'ragachaya svara' rather than the literal 'jiva svara'.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R2) and Madhyama (M1) are the stated nyasa svaras; Chatusruti Dhaivata (D2) functions as an alpa-nyasa (concluding without stress) in tara-sthayi phrases like S n d and R S n d.

raagas.name: Māyāmāḷavagauḷa
raagas.parent: 15th melakarta (Mayamalavagowla is itself the janaka/melakarta raga)
raagas.arohanam: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The very first raaga every Carnatic student learns (the sarali varisai exercises): calm, morning-fresh and devotional.
raagas.confused_with: Corresponds to Hindustani Bhairav (equivalent, not a Carnatic confusion)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G (antara gandhara, G3) and N (kakali nishada, N3).
raagas.nyasa_swaras: R (shuddha rishabha R1), M (shuddha madhyama M1) and D (shuddha dhaivata D1). Amsa swaras G and P; graha swaras S, G, D, N.

raagas.name: Mōhanaṁ
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 P D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S D2 P G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of 'Ninnukori Varnam' (Agni Natchathiram): listen for its bright, sunny pentatonic scale that skips two notes (no ma, no ni).
raagas.confused_with: Shivaranjani (same scale but with sadharana gandharam); Bilahari and Mohanakalyani (share Mohanam's arohana); Hindustani equivalent Bhoop/Bhopali
raagas.nyasa_swaras: G3, P
film_songs: Sri Ranga Ranganathanin / Nilavum Malarum (Then Nilavu, A.M. Rajah–P. Susheela)

raagas.name: Nāṭa
raagas.parent: 36th melakarta – Chalanata (Nāṭa is a janya of this mela)
raagas.arohanam: S R3 G3 M1 P D3 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 P M1 R3 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The bold, festive raaga that opens concerts, Dikshitar's 'Maha Ganapatim' and Tyagaraja's 'Jagadananda Karaka'; heroic and martial.
raagas.confused_with: Gambhiranata (Gambheera Nattai); also compared with its parent Chalanata
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Rishabha: R3 (shatsruti rishabha) is Nata's jiva svara; another reading lists R, M, N as the jiva swaras.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Sa and Pa are the principal graha/nyasa; apart from Sa and Pa, Ri and Ga are the take-off notes, with Ga (G3) also functioning as a nyasa swara.

raagas.name: Nāṭakurinji
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 M1 N2 D2 N2 P D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 M1 G3 M1 P G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A graceful, meandering raaga, a favourite for elaborate ragam-tanam-pallavi, heard in Tyagaraja's 'Manavyalakincharada'; serpentine curves.
raagas.confused_with: Ravichandrika; Kurinji (janya of Shankarabharanam)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: All swaras except R2 are jeeva swaras (and may double as nyasa); D2 and P are the strong life-notes, with G3, M1 and N2 prominent.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: P and N2 for repose (and S); R2 used sparingly, usually paired with S.
film_songs: Kavalaiyai Theerpathu Nadhiya Kalaiye (film Sivakavi) - Papanasam Sivan / G. Ramanathan

raagas.name: Pūrvīkaḷyāṇi
raagas.arohanam: S R1 G3 M2 P D2 P S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A calm, tender raaga, Dikshitar's 'Meenakshi Memudam Dehi'; soothing yet touched with a gentle, wistful longing.
raagas.confused_with: Pantuvarali/Ramakriya (shares poorvanga characteristics; distinguished by Dwisruti Rishabha and arohana vakratva)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R, M, D, N
raagas.nyasa_swaras: G, P, D
songs: Meenakshi Me Mudam Dehi, Muthuswami Dikshitar

raagas.name: Rītigauḷa
raagas.arohanam: S G2 R2 G2 M1 N2 D2 M1 N2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 M1 G2 M1 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of 'Chinna Kannan Azhaikkiran' (Kavikkuyil) and Subbaraya Sastri's 'Janani Ninnuvina': soft, meditative, winding phrases.
raagas.confused_with: Anandabhairavi and Huseni (allied ragas)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Gandhara (G2), Madhyama (M1) and Nishada (N2) are the jiva swaras, with kaisiki nishada (N2) the primary life-giving note; the phrase N2 N2 S gives the raga its unique personality, and Madhyama is a secondary life-swara.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Sa and Ma, with Ma the anchor in the lower half of the octave (one source only; other sources do not state nyasa swaras).

raagas.name: Sahānā
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 M1 P M1 D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 M1 R2 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of Tyagaraja's 'Giripai': listen for its winding, zigzag (vakra) phrases that ache with tenderness and surrender.
raagas.confused_with: Malavi; Dwijavanti (Jujavanti); historically linked to Sri raga (mela 22)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R2 (rishabham), G3 (gandharam), N2 (nishadham)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: R2 rishabham (graha/nyasa/amsa svara); dhaivatham also noted as an important rest note; gandhara is an amsa but never used as a nyasa
film_songs: Paarthen Sirithen Pakkathil Azhaithen - Veera Abhimanyu (K.V. Mahadevan)

raagas.name: Sencuruṭṭi
raagas.arohanam: D2 S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2
raagas.avarohanam: N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S N2 D2 P D2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A light, folk-flavoured raaga of thillanas and javalis with a gentle pleading lilt, heard in Oothukkadu's 'Maadu Meikkum Kanne'.
raagas.confused_with: Jhinjhoti (Hindustani, which takes sadharana gandhara G2 as a foreign note); Surutti
film_songs: En Veettu... (partial title as labelled on ragasurabhi

raagas.name: Sindhubhairavi
raagas.parent: Janya of Melakarta 8 Hanumatodi (Todi); in Hindustani music maps to Asavari thaat
raagas.arohanam: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The soulful raaga that closes concerts, Ilaiyaraaja's 'Naan Oru Sindhu' (Sindhu Bhairavi); tender pathos, bhajan-like devotion.
raagas.confused_with: Not to be confused with Sindhi Bhairavi, Sindh, Sindhura, Sindhura Bhairavi
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Gandhara (G) and Dhaivata (D) are the identity/emphasis notes (the sources label them vadi/samvadi rather than jeeva): D noteworthy in the arohana, G in the avarohana.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Panchama (P) is the named nyasa svara (Shadja is an implied universal landing).
film_songs: Sindhu Bhairavi-based songs in Muthu, Kandukondain Kandukondain

raagas.name: Suraṭi
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N2 D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 P M1 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The auspicious 'mangalam' raaga sung to bless the close of a concert, heard in Tyagaraja's 'Geetarthamu'; warm and reassuring.
raagas.confused_with: Kedaragaula (Kedara Gowlai)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Panchama (P), Nishada (N), Rishabha (R)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R)
film_songs: Alarshara Parithaapam, Swathi Thirunal (Malayalam), composer M. B. Sreenivasan, sung by K. J. Yesudas & B. Arundhathi

raagas.name: Sāma
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The serene, meditative raaga of 'Manasa Sancharare': plain, unhurried, almost ornament-free phrases that settle the mind.
raagas.confused_with: Arabhi (shares nearly the same notes; differs mainly in the nyasa swara, Sama rests on gandhara)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Madhyama (M1), Dhaivata (D2) and Gandhara (G3) are the ragachaya (identity) svaras; the soft rendering of Ma and an elongated Gandhara are Sama's speciality.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Gandhara (G3) is the classic resting note that evokes Sama (distinguishing it from Arabhi); darbar.org additionally lists Rishabha (R2) and Panchama (P).

raagas.name: Sāvēri
raagas.arohanam: S R1 M1 P D1 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A raaga of compassionate pleading (karuna), Dikshitar's 'Sri Rajagopala'; listen for its weighty, plaintive dips on ri and dha.
raagas.confused_with: Karnataka Shuddha Saveri and Malahari (share scale material)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Ri and Dha (R1, D1).
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Ma, Pa, Dha (M1, P, D1).

raagas.name: Tōḍi
raagas.parent: 8th melakarta (Hanumatodi is itself the janaka/melakarta raga)
raagas.arohanam: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The towering raaga of Oothukkadu's 'Thaaye Yashoda': vast and majestic, heavy with deep winding gamaka (oscillation).
raagas.confused_with: Not Hindustani Todi (= Carnatic Shubhapantuvarali); Carnatic Todi's Hindustani equivalent is Bhairavi thaat
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G, M, D (per karnatik.com)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: G, M, P, D, N (per karnatik.com)

raagas.name: Varāḷi
raagas.arohanam: S G1 R1 G1 M2 P D1 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D1 P M2 G1 R1 S
raagas.how_to_hear: A mystic, austere raaga, Dikshitar's 'Mamava Meenakshi'; listen for its stark, plaintive phrases evoking detachment (vairagya).
raagas.confused_with: Pantuvarali (differs only in gandharam), Subhapantuvarali (uses sadharana gandharam), Vijayasree (lacks dhaivatham), Jaganmohana
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Gandharam (G1), Madhyamam (M2), and Nishadam (N3), rendered with characteristic gamaka
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Shadjam (S), listed as the graha/amsa/nyasa swara

raagas.name: Yadukula kāṁbōji
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P D2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The gentle, serene raaga of Tyagaraja's 'Hecharikaga Rara' and Dikshitar's Saturn kriti 'Divakara Tanujam': soft, plaintive vakra phrases.
raagas.confused_with: Shuddha Saveri (symmetric pentatonic, same arohana notes); Kedaragaula (kaisiki nishadam replaces D2 in ascent)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G3 and N2 (occur only in the avarohana yet impart the raga's character); R2 (oscillated) with the signature S R M movement is central, and M is dwelt upon.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: P and S are the principal resting notes; the rakti phrase S P D S (and S S P D S in the mandra sthayi) is a special landing prayoga.

raagas.name: Ānandabhairavi
raagas.arohanam: S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 P S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: Syama Sastri's favourite soothing raaga, his 'O Jagadamba' to Goddess Kamakshi; a folk and devotional staple said to calm the mind.
raagas.confused_with: Reethigowla and Huseni (allied ragas)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Gandhara (sadharana G2) and Madhyama (shuddha M1) are the principal jeeva / life-line swaras; Ga is sung with a stress (nokku), and Panchama is also treated as a pivotal note.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Nishada and Shadja are the nyasa (resting) swaras; in alapana a relaxing halt is made on sadharana Ga and Panchama. Kaisiki Nishada (N2) is used but not dwelt upon.

raagas.name: Śankarābharaṇaṁ
raagas.parent: 29th melakarta – Dhīra Śankarābharaṇam (it is itself the mela / janaka raga)
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The Carnatic major scale (do-re-mi), raaga of the film Sankarabharanam's 'Omkara Nadanu'; grand, symmetrical, fully resolved.
raagas.jeeva_swaras: G3 (gandhara) cited as the jeeva/life note; amsa & nyasa given as G, P, S
raagas.nyasa_swaras: G3, P, S

raagas.name: Śrī
raagas.arohanam: S R2 M1 P N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 P D2 N2 P M1 R2 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The auspicious raaga that closes Tyagaraja's Pancharatna 'Endaro Mahanubhavulu': listen for its zig-zag (vakra) descending phrases.
raagas.confused_with: Madhyamavati (shares the S R2 M1 P N2 S pentatonic ascent). Note: 'Sri/Shree' is also an alternate name for Kharaharapriya itself; unrelated to Hindustani raga Shree
raagas.jeeva_swaras: Rishabha (R2, chatushruti), described as the raga's life blood and both the jiva and nyasa svara.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: Rishabha (R2), the nyasa (landing/resting) svara (the same jiva-and-nyasa statement).
film_songs: Theendai Mei Theendai, En Swasa Kaatre (1999), A. R. Rahman

raagas.name: Śrīranjani
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G2 M1 D2 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D2 M1 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The bright, cheerful six-note raaga of Tyagaraja's 'Marubalka': pleasant and uplifting, easily mistaken for its cousin Abhogi.
raagas.confused_with: Abhogi (Śrīranjani is essentially Abhogi + N2; treated as 'twin ragas'); also Jayamanohari
raagas.jeeva_swaras: R2, G2, D2, N2 are the jeeva/life swaras; of these, Gandhara (G2) and Nishada (N2) are the identity-bearing kampita notes that carry the raga's svarupa.
raagas.nyasa_swaras: M1 (madhyama), the nyasa (resting/landing) swara.

raagas.name: Ṣanmukhapriya
raagas.parent: 56th melakarta (Shanmukhapriya itself); called Chāmaram in the Dikshitar school
raagas.arohanam: S R2 G2 M2 P D1 N2 S
raagas.avarohanam: S N2 D1 P M2 G2 R2 S
raagas.how_to_hear: The raaga of 'Ooru Vittu Ooru Vandhu' (Karakattakkaran): majestic yet aching, with a dark, minor-key intensity.
raagas.confused_with: Simhendramadhyamam (melakarta 57), nearly identical scale, differing only in the nishadam (Shanmukhapriya uses N2 / kaisiki nishadam; Simhendramadhyamam uses N3)
raagas.jeeva_swaras: All the swaras are jīvaswaras (per anuradhamahesh)
raagas.nyasa_swaras: R, P and N

raagas.name: Yaman kalyāṇ
raagas.arohanam: N. R G M P D N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P M G, G m G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Tivra Ma throughout; the phrase N. R G and the leap to Ni are signatures. Sa and Pa are often skipped in the ascent.
raagas.confused_with: Bhoop (Kalyan thaat but pentatonic); Yaman-Kalyan (adds shuddh Ma). Carnatic: Kalyāṇi/Mechakalyāṇi.
raagas.pakad: N. R G, R G, P M G R, S
raagas.time: first prahar of the night (early evening)

raagas.name: Bhūp
raagas.arohanam: S R G P D S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' D P G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Pentatonic S R G P D, no Ma or Ni; serene and open.
raagas.confused_with: Deskar (same notes, different emphasis); Shuddh Kalyan. Carnatic: Mōhanaṁ / Bhoopali.
raagas.pakad: G R S D. S R G, P G, D P G R S
raagas.time: first prahar of the night (early evening)

raagas.name: Mālkauns
raagas.arohanam: S g m d n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n d m g S
raagas.how_to_hear: Komal ga, dha, ni with shuddh ma; no Re or Pa. Deep, meditative.
raagas.confused_with: Chandrakauns (shuddh Ni); Bageshri (has Re, Pa). Carnatic: Hindōḷaṁ.
raagas.pakad: m g m d, n d, m g S

raagas.name: Bhairav
raagas.arohanam: S r G m P d N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N d P m G r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Komal re and komal dha, taken with a slow andolan (oscillation); rest shuddh. Grave morning raaga.
raagas.confused_with: Ahir Bhairav; Kalingda; Ramkali. Carnatic: Māyāmāḷavagauḷa.
raagas.pakad: S r S, G m P, d P, G m r S

raagas.name: Dēś
raagas.arohanam: S R m P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D P m G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Shuddh Ni ascending, komal Ni descending; pentatonic-ish rise, fuller fall. Bright, romantic.
raagas.confused_with: Tilak Kamod, Sorath, Jaijaiwanti; Gaud Malhar. Carnatic-adjacent: Kamās.
raagas.pakad: R m P, D m G R, m G R, n. S R
raagas.time: second prahar of the night; monsoon

raagas.name: Bihāg
raagas.arohanam: N. S G m P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P M P G m G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Sweet romantic night raga on shuddh notes; the giveaway is P M G m G, a fleeting tivra Ma resolving through shuddh Ma to Ga, over a Ga-Ni frame; Re and Dha only in meend.
raagas.confused_with: Maru Bihag (tivra-Ma dominant); Bihagda; Nand. No clean Carnatic equivalent.
raagas.pakad: N. S G, m G, P M G m G, R S

raagas.name: Bāgēśrī
raagas.arohanam: n. S g m D n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D m P D m g R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Serene late-night raga; the Sa-to-Ma leap (n. S m) and the falling m g R S with komal ga/ni over a strong Ma; Pa skipped or barely touched in ascent.
raagas.confused_with: Bhimpalasi (Pa in aroha); Rageshri; Jaijaiwanti. Carnatic: Bageshri.
raagas.pakad: n. S m, g m D, m g R S

raagas.name: Darbāri
raagas.arohanam: S R g m P, d n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' d n P m P g m R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Grave, majestic midnight raga; unmistakable slow wide andolan on komal Ga and komal Dha, low-register Re-Pa emphasis.
raagas.confused_with: Adana (same swaras, faster, upper-register); Jaunpuri; Asavari. Carnatic: a Natabhairavi janya.
raagas.pakad: R g R S, m P, d n P, m P g m R S

raagas.name: Kēdār
raagas.arohanam: S m, m P, D P N D, S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P, m P D P M, m G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Opening S-m leap, both madhyams (shuddh Ma prominent, tivra Ma as ornament), Sa-Ma-Sa resting; Re and Ga dropped in ascent.
raagas.confused_with: Hameer; Kamod; Chhayanat; Maru Bihag. Carnatic: Hamir Kalyani.
raagas.pakad: S m, m P, D P M, P m, R S

raagas.name: Khamāj
raagas.arohanam: S G m P D N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D P m G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Light, romantic; the signature is the two nishads: shuddh Ni climbing, komal ni falling, with Re dropped on the way up.
raagas.confused_with: Des; Jhinjhoti; Tilak Kamod. Carnatic: Khamās.
raagas.pakad: m P D m G, n D P, m G R S

raagas.name: Mārvā
raagas.arohanam: N. D. r G M D N r' S'
raagas.avarohanam: r' N D M G r S; N. D. r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Pancham omitted and Sa barely touched, so it floats unresolved on komal Re and shuddh Dha with a mandra-Dha to komal-Re leap; yearning dusk mood.
raagas.confused_with: Puriya (same thaat, Ga-Ni emphasis); Sohni; Bhatiyar. Carnatic scale ~ Gamanashrama minus Pa.
raagas.pakad: D. r; D M G r; r G M G r S

raagas.name: Puriyā dhanaśrī
raagas.arohanam: N. r G M P; M d N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N d P M G M r G r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Purvi-family raga using ONLY tivra Ma, with komal Re/Dha and a Pancham-centred M d P ascent; plaintive after-sunset mood.
raagas.confused_with: Puriya (Marwa thaat, no Pa); Purvi (both madhyams); Gujari Todi. Carnatic: Pantuvarali/Kamavardhini.
raagas.pakad: N. r G; M d P; M G M r G; r S

raagas.name: Lalit
raagas.arohanam: N. r G m M d N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N d M m G; m G r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Rare raga juxtaposing shuddh Ma and tivra Ma directly (m-M) while omitting Pa entirely, over komal Re/Dha; serene pre-dawn mood. Gharanas differ on shuddh vs komal Dha.
raagas.confused_with: Lalit-Gauri; Sohni. Carnatic Lalita (namesake, but only shuddh Ma, no tivra Ma).
raagas.pakad: N. r G m; d M d; m G r S
raagas.time: pre-dawn / last prahar of the night

raagas.name: Basant
raagas.arohanam: S G M d N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N d P M G; M G r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Spring raga; sparse vakra ascent that skips Re and Pa and leans on taar Sa, using tivra Ma with komal Re/Dha and the M d N d P phrase.
raagas.confused_with: Paraj (closest cousin); Purvi; Puriya Dhanashri; Basant Bahar. Shares the Kamavardhini scale.
raagas.pakad: M d N d P; M G M G r S
raagas.time: spring season; also second prahar of the night

raagas.name: Śrī
raagas.arohanam: S r M P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N d P M G r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Built on the oscillating komal-Re to Pancham meend (Re-Pa sangati), skeletal ascent skipping Ga and Dha; austere devotional dusk raga. UNRELATED to the Carnatic ragam of the same name.
raagas.confused_with: Puriya Dhanashri; Purvi; Basant; Gauri. NOT the Carnatic Sri (a Kharaharapriya janya); scale ~ Kamavardhini.
raagas.pakad: N. r r P; P M G r; r S
raagas.time: late afternoon into sunset (fourth prahar of day)

raagas.name: Ahira bhairav
raagas.arohanam: S r G m P D n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D P m G r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Bhairav-like lower tetrachord with oscillating komal re, but a soft komal ni on top; komal re + komal ni, else shuddh, is the giveaway. Vadi/samvadi disputed (Ma-Sa vs Dha-Re).
raagas.confused_with: Bhairav; Nat Bhairav; Bairagi Bhairav. Carnatic: Chakravakam (exact match).
raagas.pakad: S r G m, m G r S, .n .D .n r S

raagas.name: Alahaiyā bilāval
raagas.arohanam: S R G P D N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P D n D P m G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Bright shuddh Bilaval (major scale) whose single tell is the komal ni tucked between two dhaivats descending (D n D P); ascent skips madhyam.
raagas.confused_with: plain Bilaval (no komal ni); Deshkar; Shankara. Carnatic scale: Śankarābharaṇaṁ.
raagas.pakad: G R G P, D n D P, m G R, G P D N S'

raagas.name: Tōḍī
raagas.arohanam: S r g M d N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N d P M g r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Grave, devotional late-morning raga: komal re, ati-komal ga, tivra ma, komal dha, shuddh ni. The tivra-ma + shuddh-ni signature. NOT the Carnatic raga also called Todi.
raagas.confused_with: Gujari Todi (no Pa); Multani; Bilaskhani Todi (shuddh ma + komal ni). Carnatic: Shubhapantuvarali.
raagas.pakad: .d .N S r g, M g r g, r S

raagas.name: Bilāsakhānī tōḍī
raagas.arohanam: S r g P d S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' r' n d P, d n d m g r, r g r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Plaintive Bhairavi-scale cousin of Todi (komal re, ga, dha, ni; shuddh ma) with a pentatonic S r g P d ascent and Todi-style meend on r-g. Shuddh ma + komal ni distinguish it from Miyan ki Todi.
raagas.confused_with: Bhairavi; Komal Rishabh Asavari; Miyan ki Todi. Carnatic: Hanumatōḍi (the raga Carnatic calls 'Todi').
raagas.pakad: S r g P, d m g r, g r g r S, r .n .d S

raagas.name: Bairāgi
raagas.arohanam: S r m P n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n P m r S
raagas.how_to_hear: Austere modern pentatonic (attributed to Pt. Ravi Shankar): S, komal re, shuddh ma, Pa, komal ni; no Ga, no Dha; Ma as vadi.
raagas.confused_with: Bairagi Bhairav variants (add komal dha). Carnatic: Revati (same five notes).
raagas.pakad: m P n P m r, r P m r S, .n S r S

raagas.name: Hamsadhvāni
raagas.arohanam: S R G P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N P G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Bright cheerful pentatonic, only shuddh notes, NO Ma or Dha; the G-P-N leaps and N-P-G-R-S descent are the giveaway. Vadi/samvadi cited variably.
raagas.confused_with: Shankara (adds Dha). Carnatic: Hamsadhwani (same S R G P N).
raagas.pakad: G P N S', N P G R S, .N R G P

raagas.name: Jōg
raagas.arohanam: S G m P n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n P m g S
raagas.how_to_hear: Two-gandhar oscillation: shuddh Ga in ascent, komal ga in descent resolving through the signature M g S zigzag; no Re, no Dha, komal Ni.
raagas.confused_with: Dhani (only komal ga); Jog Kauns. Carnatic near-equivalent ~ Nāṭa.
raagas.pakad: G M P n P, P n P M G M, M g S

raagas.name: Ābhōgī
raagas.arohanam: S R g m D S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' D m g R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Gentle introspective pentatonic with komal ga and shuddh Ma but NO Pa and NO Ni; komal ga approached vakra from above (m-g).
raagas.confused_with: Bhimpalasi/Dhani phrasing (but no Pa/Ni here). Carnatic: Abhogi (identical S R2 G2 M1 D2).
raagas.pakad: S R g M, g M D S', D M g R S

raagas.name: Madhukauns
raagas.arohanam: S g M P n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n P M g S
raagas.how_to_hear: Malkauns re-cast with tivra Ma and Pa in place of shuddh Ma and komal Dha; the rare tivra-Ma + komal-ni pairing. Some renditions use shuddh Ma instead, so the Ma is disputed.
raagas.confused_with: Malkauns (shuddh Ma, komal Dha, no Pa). Carnatic near-equivalent ~ Samudrapriya.
raagas.pakad: S g M P, M P g M g S, g M P n S'

raagas.name: Madhuvanti
raagas.arohanam: N. S g M P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P M g R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Sweet romantic afternoon raga with komal ga and tivra Ma; Re and Dha dropped in ascent, present in descent. Uses shuddh Re/Dha, so it does not truly fit Todi thaat.
raagas.confused_with: Multani; Bhimpalasi; Patdeep. Carnatic parent: Dharmavati (also a Carnatic raga Madhuvanti).
raagas.pakad: .N S M g M P, M g S R S

raagas.name: Miyān malhār
raagas.arohanam: N. S m R P n D N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D n P m P g m R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Serious monsoon raga in Kanada ang: the twin-nishad oscillation n D n P and the komal-ga resolution; Dha dropped in descent.
raagas.confused_with: Megh Malhar; Bahar; Gaud Malhar; Darbari/Adana (Kanada ang). No standard Carnatic equivalent.
raagas.pakad: S R, R P, g g m R S, n. D N. N. S

raagas.name: Gauḍ malhār
raagas.arohanam: S R G m R P, m P D N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D n P m G R G S
raagas.how_to_hear: Monsoon raga marked by the abrupt Re-to-Pa leap (R P) and the Gaud-ang turn G R G S; shuddh Ni ascending, komal ni descending.
raagas.confused_with: Miyan Malhar; Shuddh Malhar; Nat Malhar; Durga. No standard Carnatic equivalent.
raagas.pakad: S R G m, R P, m P D N S', D n P m, G R G S

raagas.name: Mārūbihāg
raagas.arohanam: N. S G M P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P M G M G R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Romantic Kalyan-Bihag hybrid using tivra Ma in ascent (no Re/Dha) and a shuddh-Ma touch in the descending m G P; vadi/samvadi disputed.
raagas.confused_with: Bihag (mainly shuddh Ma); Yaman/Kalyan. Carnatic: Behāg (also both madhyams).
raagas.pakad: M G, M G R S, S N. S, m G P, M G M G R S

raagas.name: Rāgēśrī
raagas.arohanam: S G m D n S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' n D m G m R S
raagas.how_to_hear: Light-romantic night raga with no Pa, shuddh Ga and komal Ni; the shuddh Gandhar and the D-G pull separate it from Bageshri (komal Ga).
raagas.confused_with: Bageshri (komal Ga); Malgunji; Bageshri-Kanada. Carnatic: Bageshri (a confusable, not exact).
raagas.pakad: n. D. n. S, G m R S, G m D n D m, G m R S

raagas.name: Śuddh sāraṅg
raagas.arohanam: N. S R M P N S'
raagas.avarohanam: S' N D P M P m R S, N. S
raagas.how_to_hear: Midday Sarang using BOTH madhyams together, the signature M m R (tivra Ma sliding to shuddh Ma) with no Ga; komal Ni used only occasionally, so its two-nishad status and time vary by gharana.
raagas.confused_with: Brindavani Sarang (no tivra Ma/Dha); Madhmad Sarang; Gaud Sarang. Carnatic: Brindavana Saranga family (no exact equivalent).
raagas.pakad: N. D. S, N. R S, M m R S, M P N S'
raagas.time: late morning to midday (second prahar of day)
